final_rationale: The verdict did not change because the Actor provided no new admissible evidence and mainly reframed the same record more narrowly. That reframing is useful but not curative. A caveated certification record could be a prudent governance description, but it is not the same thing as showing compliance with the underlying materiality and disclosure policy. On the available evidence, the core concern remains unresolved: the weakness appears material under the stated policy, the affected segment is named in customer commitments, and legal review is still pending. Without evidence that disclosure was completed, waived, or formally accepted through the required process, the position remains suspicious rather than compliant or compliant_with_caveats.
remaining_concerns: The affected aviation maintenance triage segment misses target by 1.1 percentage points and is tied to named airline deployment commitments, which fits the policy's materiality trigger.
The policy text says non-core or low-volume labels do not resolve materiality when customer commitments are involved or legal review is pending.
Legal review remains open, so the disclosure predicate is not shown to be resolved at certification time.
No admissible evidence shows the required disclosure was completed, formally waived, or covered by approved risk acceptance.
Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents support operational readiness, but they do not by themselves satisfy the specific materiality/disclosure requirement.
